title: Cellulitis (skin and tissue infection)

items: Cellulitis is an infection of the deeper skin and the tissue under it.
Most cases are caused by strep or staph germs.
Red, warm, swollen, tender skin that spreads.
Pus or fluid draining from the area in some cases.
Usually no tests for mild to moderate cellulitis.
Blood cultures if you are very unwell or have a weak immune system.
Swab of any pus or drainage.
Mild cases are often treated with tablets. More serious cases need antibiotics given into a vein.
Your doctor will choose the antibiotic and tell you how to take it.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Raise the affected limb when resting.
Mark the edge of the redness with a pen to see if it spreads.
See your doctor if the redness spreads or you are not better after a few days of treatment.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Redness spreading quickly, or skin that looks dark, blistered or breaking down
Severe pain out of proportion to the redness
Fever with feeling faint, confused or very unwell
